findings.claim: When the helper fails to start (a spawn 'error' with no 'spawn' event, or clock publication fails before actualStartedAt is set), the record mislabels the invocation as one that left the prior group state unchanged and made no new attempt. It also names the file .nonconsuming.json, although this invocation wrote the marker, charged an attempt and attempted a launch.
findings.evidence: groupConsumed now becomes true only in publishActualGroupClock (S:1529@25858ad). consumeGroup writes the marker (S:1556), and commandLaunchAttempted=true is set before spawn (S:1346). On a spawn error the receipt has cleanupProven false and S:2047 throws. Then priorConsumptionNotRestored = marker exists && !actualStartedAt is true (S:2137). That gives groupConsumed:null and priorGroupState PRIOR_GROUP_CONSUMPTION_NOT_RESTORED (S:2154-2155), continuation PRIOR_GROUP_STATE_UNCHANGED_NO_NEW_ATTEMPT (S:2189), and path G-<inv>.nonconsuming.json (S:2202), with no G.group.json. At cc584f9 this path wrote .group.json.
findings.fix: Set priorConsumptionNotRestored only when the marker predates this invocation (!run.markerWrittenByInvocation). Label the current case explicitly, for example LAUNCH_ATTEMPTED_SPAWN_NOT_OBSERVED_CLEANUP_UNCERTAIN, with a distinct file name or a terminal group record. Change no limit.

findings.claim: A transient failure to publish the invocation witness strands the group permanently with nothing launched, yet the record is labelled clean (cleanupProven:true, evidenceUncertain:false) and the lock is released. This is outside the stated rule that only uncertainty, consumption or fixture failure is permanent.
findings.evidence: initializeInvocationHistory is the first statement in the try (S:1954). Its writeNew (S:1478-1479) can throw at openSync 'wx' (S:48, for example EMFILE, an antivirus lock or EACCES) before any .pending file exists. In that case run.invocationWitness stays null (S:1939). The catch does not set evidenceUncertain, so cleanupProven is true, cleanZeroLaunchRefusal is false (S:2140), the continuation is TERMINAL_NO_AUTOMATIC_REPEAT (S:2193), the reservation disposition is OWNED_CHILD_ABSENCE_ESTABLISHED… (S:2187) and the lock is released (S:2207). Every later fresh start then reaches readInvocationWitness on the null pointer (S:1871) and fails the plain check 'raw invocation witness missing' (S:1582). That refusal is permanent and not sticky-labelled. For G0, this would lose the window.
findings.fix: Treat witness-publication failure as evidence uncertainty (sticky, lock held, labelled as such). Alternatively, let the guard accept a clean record with a null witness and no progress (no attempt, receipts or folder) under the material-change binding. Raise no limit.

findings.claim: A transient failure while inspecting the invocation budget during finalization is reported as an exhausted limit. For a started non-G0 group, it turns a pausable state into a permanent terminal group result, and that result stops the rest of the run. Neither effect is disclosed.
findings.evidence: invocationBudgetState is wrapped in try/catch, and a throw sets inspectionFailure (S:2117-2119). That pushes INVOCATION_BUDGET_UNVERIFIED (S:2124-2125). A zero-launch record is then labelled NONCONSUMING_UNSTARTED_LIMIT_EXHAUSTED_NO_RESET (S:2185, S:2193), although the guard still accepts it and a later invocation may proceed. For a started group, paused requires limits.length===0 (S:2135), so the result is written to G.group.json (S:2202) with TERMINAL_GROUP_FAILURE… (S:2186). invocationBudgetState then lists that group as terminal (S:1814-1815), and RUN_STOPPED_BY_TERMINAL_GROUP refuses all later groups (S:1826-1828). This fails closed, but a single EBUSY on readdir, stat or read at that instant ends the run.
findings.fix: Give an inspection failure its own label (for example ELIGIBILITY_UNVERIFIED_NOT_EXHAUSTED) and disclose that it is terminal for a started group. Alternatively, write a non-terminal hold that still preserves the pause evidence, leaving the resume to re-run assertInvocationBudget. Do not change the nine-invocation cap.

closureOpinion.item: Per-group timing arithmetic (zero-launch restart and pause)
closureOpinion.note:
In all eight groups, commands + setup + admission + finalization equal the wall exactly: G0 51000+9000; G1, G2, G5, G6 480000+120000; G3, G4 720000+180000; G7 1200000+300000.

- Zero-launch restart: the time test reduces to A−f ≥ remaining reserve, because the wall covers the reserve whenever spent ≥ 0. Only the aggregate, the cap or wait capacity can block it.
- Post-spawn work is at most W−setup.
- Pause: needs (completed ceilings + waits spent) − (f − actual start) ≥ allowance. That is 30000 for G1, 45000 for G4 and 75000 for G7. G2, G3, G5 and G6 have one child and never pause.

First slices are G0 428, G1 15000, G2–G6 30000, G7 25000, matching M:798-848.
